content.json:
# Telecom MCP tools

Generated from the KPI and SLO catalogues by `scripts/generate_observability.py`. Every tile below states the question it answers and what it means when it moves.

## Tool calls

How much work is this thing doing?

The denominator for every ratio below. A sudden fall is an outage upstream of us and is worth more attention than a rise.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = count()
content.title: Tool calls

content.json:
## Success ratio

Are calls working?

Successful and deduplicated calls over all calls. Deduplicated counts as success because the caller got the answer they asked for.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome in ("ok"))) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Success ratio

content.json:
## Failure ratio

Are we breaking?

Calls that were authorized and then failed. This is our fault or the middleware's; a denial or a guardrail block is not counted here, because a control working correctly is not an error.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "failed")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Failure ratio

content.json:
## Latency p95

Is it fast enough for a live call?

A voice case has a five minute budget and an agent may need several tools inside it. p95 is the number that decides whether that is possible.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = percentile(duration, 95) / 1000.0
content.title: Latency p95

content.json:
## Latency p99

How bad is the tail?

The customer who is already annoyed is in this bucket. Track it separately from p95: a p95 that holds while p99 doubles is a retry storm.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = percentile(duration, 99) / 1000.0
content.title: Latency p99

content.json:
## Calls over the time budget

How many calls blew the ten second budget?

Observations above the last histogram bucket. A quantile hides these; a count does not, and this is the one number that maps to a real customer sitting in silence.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = countif(duration > 10000)
content.title: Calls over the time budget

content.json:
## Load shed ratio

Are we refusing work because we are full?

Shedding is the designed behaviour under load, not a bug, but a non-zero value means capacity is the constraint and the next step is replicas.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "shed")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Load shed ratio

content.json:
## Deduplication ratio

How often is a caller repeating itself?

A small number is the idempotency store doing its job. A large one is an agent retrying because it thinks we failed, which is a latency problem wearing a different hat.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "deduplicated")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Deduplication ratio

content.json:
## Backend retry ratio

Is the middleware healthy?

Attempts beyond the first, over all attempts. Rises before failures do, which makes it the earliest honest warning we have.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "failed")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Backend retry ratio

content.json:
## Authorization denial ratio

How much is the kernel refusing?

A steady low number is normal: agents probe tools they do not hold scopes for. A step change means a token, a role or a claim namespace changed, and it will usually have changed by accident.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "denied")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Authorization denial ratio

content.json:
## Guardrail block ratio

What are the guardrails stopping?

Near zero is expected and is not a reason to relax anything. A spike in the injection stage is an attack or a bad prompt template; a spike in argument_size is usually a client bug.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | summarize value = todouble(countif(outcome == "guardrail_blocked")) / todouble(max_of(count(), 1))
content.title: Guardrail block ratio

content.json:
## Output guardrail blocks

Did we nearly hand a secret to the model?

This should be zero forever. Any non-zero value means a write happened and the response was withheld, and it is a page rather than a ticket: redaction has met a field it does not know about.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | where stage startswith "output_" | summarize value = count()
content.title: Output guardrail blocks

content.json:
## Tickets created

What did the agent actually do for people?

Up is not automatically good. Read it beside the callback and refund numbers: more tickets and fewer callbacks is the agent resolving things.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | where tool == "create_support_ticket" and outcome == "ok" | summarize value = count()
content.title: Tickets created

content.json:
## Callbacks scheduled

How often does this end with a human ringing back?

The closest thing to a containment measure we have. A rise means the agent is handing more away, which may be correct and is never neutral.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | where tool == "schedule_callback" and outcome == "ok" | summarize value = count()
content.title: Callbacks scheduled

content.json:
## Refund approvals requested

How much money is queued behind a supervisor?

Nothing has moved when this increments; it is a queue depth for humans. Watch it against the action budget: a rise in both is one case looping.

content.query:
let calls = dependencies
    | where name == "execute_tool"
    | where timestamp > ago({TimeRange})
    | extend outcome = tostring(customDimensions["outcome"]),
             tool = tostring(customDimensions["tool"]),
             stage = tostring(customDimensions["stage"]);
calls | where tool == "request_refund_approval" and outcome == "ok" | summarize value = count()
content.title: Refund approvals requested
